title: Robust Linear Dueling Bandits with Post-serving Context under Unknown Delays and Adversarial Corruptions
topic: General Machine Learning->Online Learning, Active Learning and Bandits
claim: Our method's regret grows far more slowly than all baselines, showing consistent robustness across both corruption settings.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared legend style, error bars on curves
description: Two side-by-side line charts plot cumulative regret (y-axis, 0 to about 3500) against rounds t (x-axis, 0 to 2000). Panel (a) is labeled Strategic and panel (b) is labeled Stochastic. Each panel has a legend in the upper left with five methods: RCDP-UCB (Ours) in thick blue, RCDB in green, ColSTIM in orange, MaxInP in purple, and MaxPairUCB in red. The orange, purple and red curves climb steeply and almost linearly to about 3000 to 3400 in (a) and 2400 to 3000 in (b). The green RCDB curve reaches about 1500 to 1600. The blue curve flattens early and ends near 900 to 950. Vertical error bars mark each curve at regular intervals. The eye goes first to the blue line sitting well below the others.
caption: Performance comparison without post-serving contexts, i.e., the linear setting (C = 25, Λ = 104, µτ = 100, σ = 10; 10 runs). RCDP-UCB consistently outperforms RCDB, demonstrating the robustness of our unified weighting mechanism.
abstract: We study linear dueling bandits in volatile environments characterized by the simultaneous presence of post-serving contexts, delayed feedback, and adversarial corruption. Feedback is subject to unknown stochastic or adversarial delays and a cumulative corruption budget $\mathcal{C}$. To address these challenges, we propose e RCDP-UCB, which integrates a learned approximator that predicts post-serving contexts from pre-serving information. It further employs an adaptive weighting strategy that clips feature vectors to mitigate the impact of corrupted and delayed observations simultaneously. Under standard regularity conditions and a parametric post-serving mapping, we rigorously establish that our algorithm is delay-regime-agnostic, achieving a regret upper bound of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(d(\sqrt{T} + \mathcal{C} + \mathcal{D}))$, where $d$ is the total feature dimension and $\mathcal{D}$ encapsulates the delay complexity. Crucially, our analysis reveals an additive cost structure between corruption and delay, avoiding the multiplicative degradation typical of prior works. We further establish lower bounds that nearly match our upper bounds up to a $\sqrt{d}$ factor for adversarial delays in the absence of post-serving contexts. Code is available at https://github.com/youngmin0oh/rcdp-public.
